summary: The paper implements Grover-based portfolio selection circuits using QES and Grover Adaptive Search on Qiskit simulators. Experiments use a toy dataset of 8 efficient portfolios, requiring 18 qubits for the single‑list maximum‑search circuit and 37 qubits for the two‑list conditional slicing oracle with resolving power d=0.01. Results demonstrate correct selection of threshold‑filtered portfolios and the maximum Sharpe ratio but only on noiseless simulators.

experiments.description: Grover-based conditional slicing to select efficient portfolios whose returns exceed a threshold and standard deviations fall below a threshold, implemented with QES and tested on Qiskit simulators.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Exponential Search (QES) with explicit threshold oracles for portfolio selection
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Threshold values supplied from classical efficient-frontier outputs; QES starts with m=1 and random j in [0,m).

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Eight portfolio return values and eight standard-deviation values are encoded in registers; values are treated as phase-encoded decimals in [0,1) and compared via a GT-gate. The search space size is N=8, so 3 qubits encode the index register.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Select portfolios satisfying r_k > S1 and sigma_k < S2 (conditional slicing on efficient portfolios).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Oracle marks states satisfying the threshold conditions; QES is used to find a marked item. No penalty formulation.

problem_instance.description: Selection among a subsample of efficient portfolios using return and standard-deviation thresholds.

dataset_specification.description: Subsample of efficient portfolios; returns and standard deviations each reduced to 8 values. Risk-return pairs are assumed available as input from classical mean-variance optimization.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical mean-variance optimization with no-short-selling is used to generate efficient portfolios; values are restricted to [0,1) and integer parts are not compared.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Implemented and tested on simulators; success described qualitatively, with time-out used for the M=0 case.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate efficient frontier classically; subsample to 8 return and 8 standard-deviation values; choose resolving power d=0.01.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure output and interpret as selected portfolio; time-out used when no solution exists.

speedup_claims.conditions: for Grover-based conditional slicing with QES; assuming M marked solutions and access to explicit threshold oracles
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports simulator implementation and theoretical oracle/query complexity, not wall-clock speedup on hardware.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated; experiment uses N=8 portfolios.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require large N lists and fault-tolerant Grover oracles capable of evaluating portfolio thresholds at scale; current implementation uses only 37 qubits and simulator execution.
limiting_factors: Only demonstrated on a simulator with N=8 portfolios
Oracle construction requires phase encoding of classical data
No comparison against optimized classical search
State preparation and data loading dominate cost

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the circuits were implemented using IBM's Qiskit SDK simulators and no physical QPU is named.
18 qubits reported from 3 index qubits plus 15 qubits for the GT-gate at resolving power d=0.01.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only gate scaling and qubit counts are given.
The paper reports theoretical Grover complexity O(sqrt(N/M)) but performs only small-scale simulator demonstrations.
No empirical comparison with classical algorithms is presented.

experiments.description: Grover Adaptive Search to find the portfolio with the maximum Sharpe ratio among efficient portfolios, implemented with Qiskit simulators.

algorithm.variant: Grover Adaptive Search (GAS) for maximum Sharpe ratio
algorithm.convergence_criteria: After c GAS repetitions, success probability is at least 1 - 1/2^c.
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial threshold is a randomly chosen list value; later thresholds are updated from QES outcomes.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Sharpe ratios for 8 portfolios are encoded; 3 qubits encode the index register and 15 qubits are used for the GT-gate at d=0.01.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find the portfolio index with maximum Sharpe ratio.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: GAS iteratively updates the threshold to the best-known value and uses QES as a subroutine.

problem_instance.description: Maximum Sharpe-ratio search over a subsample of efficient portfolios.

dataset_specification.description: Subsample of efficient portfolios; Sharpe ratios computed with a 0% risk-free rate.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Sharpe ratios are calculated classically from the efficient portfolios; all values are in [0,1).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Implemented and tested on simulators; successful retrieval of the highest Sharpe-ratio portfolio is reported qualitatively.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical Sharpe-ratio computation from efficient portfolios
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute Sharpe ratios classically using a 0% risk-free rate; select a random initial threshold value from the list.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure the index of the maximum Sharpe-ratio portfolio; GAS repeats c times to boost success probability.

classical_baselines.method_name: classical Sharpe-ratio computation from efficient portfolios

speedup_claims.conditions: for Grover Adaptive Search on an unsorted list of portfolio Sharpe ratios; assuming threshold updates via QES
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports theoretical O(sqrt(N)) query complexity and simulator-based implementation, but no empirical runtime comparison.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated; tested with N=8 portfolios.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault-tolerant Grover Adaptive Search over large financial datasets with efficient Sharpe-ratio oracle evaluation.
limiting_factors: Very small toy problem size (8 portfolios)
Oracle requires classical preprocessing and encoding

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the circuits were implemented using IBM's Qiskit SDK simulators and no physical QPU is named.
18 qubits reported from 3 index qubits plus 15 qubits for the GT-gate at resolving power d=0.01.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only gate scaling and qubit counts are given.
The authors demonstrate successful retrieval of the maximum Sharpe ratio on a simulator but provide no empirical classical comparison.
The claimed benefit is the theoretical O(sqrt(N)) Grover speedup.
